title: Milan: DECISION DAY - incline intervals or bike intervals
terrain: treadmill 10-12% incline or indoor bike, zero descent

steps.target: Z4 at 10-12% incline, or bike Z4, 88-94% LTHR

coachNotes: OPTIMAL LOAD RULE, THE GOVERNING GATE FROM 24 AUG: a session passes only if it produces no symptoms during it, none immediately after, and none the next day. Any one of the three is a fail, and the next session drops back to the last level that passed. The ceiling during a run is 2/10 with no spike afterwards; mild is allowed, new or worsening is not. This replaces every softer wording elsewhere in this plan. GAIT, MEASURED FROM THE 22 AUG CADENCE STREAM ON 24 AUG. Your descent cadence is already good and is NOT the problem: 177 spm on grades steeper than -20%, 179 spm across the second half of the sustained descents, 176 on the final descent to the door. Do not change it, and do not let anyone tell you to. THE EXPOSURE IS FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL: 152 spm on flat ground and 156 spm at -3 to -10%. That is precisely the gradient band where the knee spends longest inside the 20-30 degree compression zone under load, it is the running you do most of, and the final 1250m into Bansko is full of it. TARGET 165-170 spm ON FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL, a 5-10% lift, which is the range the gait-retraining literature uses. Metronome or a 165 bpm playlist. Shorter steps at the same effort; do not convert it into more pace. STEP WIDTH: run slightly wider than feels natural, not on a tightrope. Narrow step width raises ITB strain and strain rate directly and it is one of the few things you can change inside 19 days. THIS IS THE DECISION POINT FOR 5 SEPTEMBER AND FOR THE WEEKEND, so run the numbers honestly tonight rather than hoping. GREEN, meaning 48 hours of walking with zero pins and a negative Noble test: do this on the treadmill at 10-12%, and Saturday's dune repeats come back on. AMBER, meaning pins have faded but are not gone: bike version at the same load, and Saturday stays flat. RED, meaning pins unchanged or worse, or a positive Noble: bike only for the rest of the week, and we have a different conversation about 12 September. CUT FROM 5x5min TO 5x4min AND FROM 85 TO 75. The week lost its eccentric strength block, which was its main justification for a hard day, and there is no fitness to chase at CTL 43 against a 42 target. What this session is still worth keeping for is the climbing-specific intensity, which transfers directly to 1900m of continuous ascent off the gun at Pirin, and which costs the band nothing when it is done uphill or on a bike. Hold the gradient or the resistance fixed and drop the speed if HR runs over 94%. Rep five should look like rep one. HIP BLOCK AFTER, second and last one before you travel. HIP BLOCK, THIS IS THE ACTUAL ITBS INTERVENTION AND IT GOES AHEAD: side-lying hip abduction 3x15 per side, clamshells 3x15 per side, single-leg glute bridges 3x12 per side, side plank with top-leg abduction 3x30s per side, Copenhagen planks 3x20s per side, single-leg calf raises 3x15. Hip abductor weakness with contralateral pelvic drop is the mechanism that lets the band compress the lateral epicondyle, and strengthening it is the one gym intervention with real evidence behind it. OUT THIS WEEK, NO NEGOTIATION: step-downs, split squats, walking lunges, anything that loads a bent knee through 20-40 degrees. Step-downs load precisely the flexion band that is currently symptomatic. Nordics are out too, not because they provoke the band but because there is no reason to add novel soreness in a week we are trying to read a signal through. SELF-CARE: do not foam-roll the IT band itself, you are compressing a structure whose problem is compression. Roll the TFL at the front of the hip, the glutes, and the outer quad above the knee. Ice the lateral knee 10 minutes after training.
